# Overview



**IDPForge** (Intrinsically Disordered Protein, FOlded and disordered Region GEnerator) is a transformer-based protein language diffusion model that generates all-atom structural ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) that maintain their folded domains. It operates by jointly diffusing backbone translations in **ℝ³**, backbone rotations in **SO(3)** via the IGSO(3) distribution, and sidechain torsion angles — then learning to denoise this composite structure with a recycling transformer network adapted from ESMFold. The result is a physics-validated, experimentally-guidable ensemble of conformers that captures the conformational heterogeneity intrinsic to disordered sequences.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L5), [setup.py](/setup.py#L1-L23)

## Why IDPForge?

Traditional structure prediction tools like AlphaFold2 and ESMFold excel at folded proteins but produce single static structures that misrepresent disordered regions — often collapsing them into low-confidence, non-physical conformations. IDPForge addresses this fundamental gap by treating disorder as a **distribution over structures** rather than a single prediction. It generates diverse, physically plausible conformers that collectively represent the conformational ensemble of a disordered protein or region, enabling downstream biophysical analysis, experimental validation, and ensemble reweighting.

The following table summarizes IDPForge's positioning relative to related tools:

| Capability | AlphaFold2 / ESMFold | RFdiffusion | **IDPForge** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Folded structure prediction | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (template-fixed) |
| IDP/IDR ensemble generation | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| SE(3) backbone diffusion | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| SO(3) IGSO(3) rotational diffusion | ❌ | Partial | ✅ |
| Torsion angle diffusion | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Experimental guidance (PRE, Rg) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Folded-domain preservation | N/A | ❌ | ✅ |
| AMBER relaxation + repair | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| X-EISD ensemble scoring | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L1-L5), [idpforge/model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L1-L50)

## Architecture at a Glance

IDPForge's architecture threads together three diffusion processes, a recycling transformer denoiser, and a multi-stage post-processing pipeline into a unified generation workflow:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Diffusion["Diffusion Process (Forward)"]
        SE3["SE(3) Translation<br/>EuclideanDiffuser<br/>ℝ³ backbone positions"]
        SO3["SO(3) Rotation<br/>IGSO3<br/>Backbone frame orientations"]
        TOR["Torsion Diffusion<br/>TorsionDiffuser<br/>χ₁–χ₄ sidechain angles"]
    end

    subgraph Denoiser["Transformer Denoiser (Reverse)"]
        EMB["Input Embedding<br/>Time + AA + SS + Torsion"]
        PAIR["Pairwise Encoding<br/>Geometric 2D features"]
        TRUNK["FoldingTrunk<br/>Recycling attention blocks"]
        IPA["Structure Module<br/>IPA + ResNet + Angle pred"]
    end

    subgraph PostProc["Post-Processing Pipeline"]
        AMBER["AMBER Relaxation<br/>ff14SB minimization"]
        REPAIR["Structure Repair<br/>Chirality + HIS ring fix"]
        VALID["Validation<br/>Clash + Bond + Knot check"]
    end

    subgraph Scoring["Ensemble Scoring"]
        XEISD["X-EISD<br/>Log-likelihood scoring"]
    end

    SE3 --> EMB
    SO3 --> PAIR
    TOR --> EMB
    EMB --> TRUNK
    PAIR --> TRUNK
    TRUNK --> IPA
    IPA --> AMBER
    AMBER --> REPAIR
    REPAIR --> VALID
    VALID --> XEISD

    style Diffusion fill:#e8f4f8,stroke:#2196F3
    style Denoiser fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#FF9800
    style PostProc fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#4CAF50
    style Scoring fill:#f3e5f5,stroke:#9C2770
```

Sources: [idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L400-L599), [idpforge/model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L53-L130)

## Core Model: The IDPForge Transformer

The `IDPForge` module is the central neural network that predicts clean structures from noised inputs. Its forward pass constructs a **single-sequence representation** `s_s_0` by summing three embedding streams — sinusoidal **timestep embeddings**, **amino acid type** embeddings, and **secondary structure** embeddings — then feeds these through an MLP into the trunk's sequence state dimension. A **pairwise representation** `s_z_0` is built from geometric 2D features (distance and angle bins) derived from the noised backbone coordinates `x_t`. Both representations pass through the `FoldingTrunk`, which applies alternating triangular self-attention and transition blocks with optional **recycling** (up to 3 iterations by default). The trunk's structure module then produces SE(3) frames, sidechain frames, and torsion angles via Invariant Point Attention (IPA).

> [!TIP]
> During inference, the `recon` method iterates backward from timestep T→0, calling `forward` at each step and delegating coordinate/torsion updates to the `Denoiser`. When a **folded template** is provided, residues in the folded mask are pinned to timestep 0 at every reverse step — this is how IDPForge preserves folded domain geometry while sampling only disordered regions.

Sources: [idpforge/model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L53-L200), [idpforge/model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L130-L283)

## The Three Diffusion Processes

IDPForge diffuses protein structure along three complementary channels, each with its own noise schedule and reverse-time denoising formula:

| Diffusion Space | Class | Forward Process | Reverse Update | Key Parameters |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ℝ³ Translations** | `EuclideanDiffuser` | Linear β-schedule on Cα positions | Analytic Gaussian transition `μ(x_t, x̂_0, t)` | `euclid_b0=0.01`, `euclid_bT=0.06` |
| **SO(3) Rotations** | `IGSO3` | Sample from IGSO(3) at increasing σ(t) | Score-based reverse SDE on SO(3) tangent space | `min_b=1.5`, `max_b=2.5`, cached CDF |
| **Torsion Angles** | `TorsionDiffuser` | Linear β-schedule on χ₁–χ₄ in [−π, π) | Wrapped Gaussian with analytic μ, σ | `torsion_b0=0.01`, `torsion_bT=0.06` |

The `Diffuser` class orchestrates all three: given a clean pose, it returns a trajectory of diffused backbone coordinates `[T, L, 5, 3]`, rigid frames `[T, L, 4, 4]`, and torsion encodings `[T, L, 4, 2]` (sin/cos pairs). The `Denoiser` class handles the reverse direction, combining the model's predicted `x̂_0` with the current `x_t` using the analytic posterior for translations and torsions, and the IGSO(3) score approximation for rotations.

Sources: [idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L1-L200), [idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L200-L400)

## Two Sampling Modes

IDPForge provides two distinct sampling entry points that reflect the two fundamental use cases:

**Fully Disordered Proteins** (`sample_idp.py`) — Given a bare amino acid sequence, generates a complete IDP ensemble from scratch. Secondary structure annotations are either fetched from a pre-built database or defaulted to all-coil. The entire chain is diffused and denoised with no template constraints.

**IDRs with Folded Domains** (`sample_ldr.py`) — Given a pre-built `.npz` template (created by `mk_ldr_template.py`), samples only the disordered region while keeping folded residues fixed. The template supplies frozen backbone coordinates, torsion angles, and a binary mask. At each reverse timestep, masked residues are reset to their template values (timestep 0), ensuring the folded domain remains unperturbed. This mode also supports attention chunking for long sequences and coordinate offsets for multi-conformer templates.

Sources: [sample_idp.py](/sample_idp.py#L1-L80), [sample_ldr.py](/sample_ldr.py#L1-L100)

## Post-Processing and Validation

Raw diffusion outputs undergo a rigorous three-phase pipeline before being admitted into the final ensemble:

1. **AMBER Relaxation** — Energy minimization with the ff14SB force field. Folded-domain residues are harmonically restrained; IDR residues and junctions relax freely. Configurable via `max_iterations`, `stiffness`, and `tolerance` in `configs/sample.yml`.
2. **Repair** — Detects and corrects D-amino acid chirality inversions and broken histidine ring bonds introduced during relaxation. Repaired structures are re-relaxed.
3. **Validation** — Unified checks for chirality integrity, bond lengths/angles, clash scores (with adaptive smart thresholds), and backbone topology via knot detection. Only structures passing all checks are renamed to `N_validated.pdb`.

This loop (Generate → Relax → Repair → Validate) repeats until the target conformer count is reached, with state persisted for recovery from interruptions.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L268-L290), [configs/sample.yml](/configs/sample.yml#L42-L57)

## Ensemble Scoring with X-EISD

The `score_ensemble.py` script and the `scoring/` module provide integrated X-EISD (Experimental Inferential Structure Determination) ensemble scoring. Given an ensemble of PDB structures and experimental data, it back-calculates observables and reports per-property MAE and X-EISD log-likelihood:

| Observable | Flag | Back-Calculation Method | External Dependency |
|---|---|---|---|
| J-couplings | `--jc` | Karplus equation | None (Biopython) |
| NOE distances | `--noe` | Inverse 6th power average | None |
| PRE distances | `--pre` | Inverse 6th power average | None |
| smFRET | `--fret` | Inter-dye distance | None |
| Chemical shifts | `--cs` | UCBShift (CSpred) | Separate conda env |

The default benchmark protocol runs 30 trials of 100-conformer subsamples, producing `scores_trials.csv`. The `--normalize` flag aggregates cross-method comparison tables.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L330-L380), [scoring/scorer.py](/scoring/scorer.py#L1-L136)

## AlphaFlex Pipeline

The `AlphaFlex/` directory provides an end-to-end automated pipeline (AFX-IDPForge) for batch-processing proteins from the AlphaFold2 database:

| Step | Script | Function |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Step_1_case_label.py` | Classify each IDR as Tail, Linker, or Loop; assign category labels |
| 1B | `Step_1B_subset_label.py` | Filter proteins by length, IDR type counts, and IDR length ranges |
| 2 | `Step_2_mk_ldr_template.py` | Build per-IDR templates (frozen fold + dynamic IDR placement) |
| 3 | `Step_3_sample_conformer.py` | Generate validated conformers per IDR via the diffusion loop |
| 4 | `Step_4_ldr_stitch.py` | Monte Carlo stitch multi-IDR proteins; minimize and validate |

Step 4's Monte Carlo stitching is particularly noteworthy for multi-IDR proteins: it sequentially grafts sampled IDR conformers onto folded domains by aligning overlapping junction residues, then performs full-structure AMBER minimization with restraints on folded regions.

Sources: [AlphaFlex/README.md](/AlphaFlex/README.md#L1-L80), [AlphaFlex/README.md](/AlphaFlex/README.md#L80-L146)

## Project Structure

```
IDPForge/
├── idpforge/                     # Core library
│   ├── model.py                  # IDPForge transformer network
│   ├── wrapper.py                # PyTorch Lightning training wrapper
│   ├── loader.py                 # Diffusion dataset & data module
│   ├── loss.py                   # FAPE, torsion, distance, violation losses
│   ├── esm_wrapper.py            # ESM2 embedding integration
│   ├── misc.py                   # I/O utilities (PDB output, input processing)
│   └── utils/
│       ├── diff_utils.py         # Diffuser, Denoiser, EuclideanDiffuser, IGSO3, TorsionDiffuser
│       ├── igso3_utils.py        # IGSO(3) numerical computation & Exp map
│       ├── tensor_utils.py       # Geometric tensor ops (dihedrals, t2d, alignment)
│       ├── potential.py          # Experimental guidance potentials (PRE, Rg)
│       ├── pre_relax.py          # Pre-relaxation repair
│       ├── relax.py              # AMBER relaxation engine
│       ├── structure_repair.py   # D-amino acid & HIS ring repair
│       ├── structure_validation.py  # Unified validation checks
│       └── validation_metrics.py # Rg and per-group distance metrics
├── esm/                          # Refactored ESM2 modules (attention, trunk)
├── scoring/                      # X-EISD ensemble scoring modules
├── AlphaFlex/                    # Automated AFX-IDPForge pipeline (Steps 1–4)
├── configs/
│   ├── sample.yml                # Sampling configuration
│   └── train.yml                 # Training configuration
├── dockerfiles/                  # Docker & Apptainer recipes (Ampere/Blackwell)
├── sample_idp.py                 # Entry point: fully disordered protein sampling
├── sample_ldr.py                 # Entry point: IDR with folded template sampling
├── mk_ldr_template.py            # Template builder for IDR sampling
├── mk_flex_template.py           # Template builder for linker IDR sampling
├── score_ensemble.py             # X-EISD ensemble scoring entry point
├── train.py                      # Training entry point
├── environment.yml               # Conda environment specification
└── setup.py                      # Package installation (v1.1.0)
```

Sources: [setup.py](/setup.py#L1-L23), [idpforge/model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L1-L50)

## Training Overview

Training uses PyTorch Lightning with the `IDPForgeWrapper`, which wraps the core model with an **Exponential Moving Average (EMA)** of parameters (decay=0.99), an **AlphaFold-style learning rate scheduler** with warmup and step decay, and a composite loss function. The data pipeline (`IDPloader`) loads pickled structure datasets, applies the full forward diffusion at training time, and samples timesteps with a linear weighting that emphasizes later (noisier) steps. Self-conditioning is applied stochastically: with 50% probability, the model's own prediction at timestep t+1 is fed as an additional input at timestep t. The composite training loss combines **FAPE** (frame-aligned point error), **angular** (torsion), **distance** (Cβ–Cβ), and **violation** terms, with distance and violation losses activated only after configurable epoch thresholds.

Sources: [train.py](/train.py#L1-L80), [idpforge/wrapper.py](/idpforge/wrapper.py#L1-L100), [idpforge/loss.py](/idpforge/loss.py#L1-L70)

> [!TIP]
> Model weights and example data are distributed via Figshare. The released checkpoint uses EMA weights (`pl_sd["ema"]["params"]`), not the raw training weights. When loading, the `openfold` version is checked to handle a key renaming (`points.` → `points.linear.`) introduced in openfold v2+.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L200-L210), [sample_idp.py](/sample_idp.py#L40-L55)

# Quick Start



Get IDPForge running on your machine — from cloning the repository to generating your first intrinsically disordered protein (IDP) ensemble. This guide walks through environment setup, weight acquisition, and your first sampling commands in under 15 minutes.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, ensure your system meets these requirements:

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| **GPU** | NVIDIA GPU (sm_60–sm_80 for default install; newer GPUs may need the alternative CUDA 12.8 path) |
| **CUDA** | 12.1 (default) or 12.8 (alternative) |
| **Conda** | Miniconda or Anaconda with `mamba` optional for faster resolves |
| **Disk** | ~15 GB for environment + model weights + OpenFold |
| **Git** | For cloning IDPForge and OpenFold |

## Installation

The full installation has three phases: **clone → environment → OpenFold**. The diagram below maps the complete flow:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["git clone IDPForge"] --> B["conda env create -f environment.yml"]
    B --> C["conda activate IDPForge"]
    C --> D["pip install -e . (IDPForge)"]
    D --> E["cd ../ && git clone openfold"]
    E --> F["Download stereo_chemical_props.txt"]
    F --> G["Copy openfold_setup_12.1.py → setup.py"]
    G --> H["pip install -e . (OpenFold)"]
    H --> I["Download weights from Figshare"]
    I --> J["✅ Ready to sample"]

    style A fill:#4a90d9,color:#fff
    style J fill:#2d8b4e,color:#fff
```

### Step 1 — Clone IDPForge

```bash
git clone https://github.com/THGLab/IDPForge.git
cd IDPForge
```

### Step 2 — Create the Conda Environment

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate IDPForge
pip install -e .
```

The default `environment.yml` installs **PyTorch 2.5.1 + CUDA 12.1**. If you have newer GPUs (released after Q4 2025) and encounter compatibility issues, switch to the alternative by editing four marked lines in `environment.yml`: `cuda-toolkit=12.8`, `cuda-version=12.8`, `--extra-index-url` to `cu128`, and `torch==2.7.1`.

> [!TIP]
> The environment includes DeepSpeed, PyTorch Lightning, OpenMM, MDTraj, and MMseqs2 — all required for the full training-sampling-relaxation-validation pipeline.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L15-L41), [environment.yml](/environment.yml#L1-L82)

### Step 3 — Install OpenFold

IDPForge depends on OpenFold utilities for protein I/O and feature computation. Clone it **in the same parent directory** as IDPForge:

```bash
cd ../
git clone https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold.git
cd openfold/openfold/resources
wget https://git.scicore.unibas.ch/schwede/openstructure/-/raw/7102c63615b64735c4941278d92b554ec94415f8/modules/mol/alg/src/stereo_chemical_props.txt
cd ../../
```

Then replace the OpenFold `setup.py` with the patched version from IDPForge and install:

```bash
cp path/to/my/IDPForge/dockerfiles/openfold_setup_12.1.py path/to/my/openfold/setup.py
pip install -e .
```

> If you used the CUDA 12.8 alternative, copy `openfold_setup_12.8.py` instead.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L43-L98)

### Step 4 — Download Model Weights and Data

Download pretrained weights, example data, and inference inputs from [Figshare](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.28414937). Place the `weights/` directory directly into `IDPForge/weights/` and merge the contents of the downloaded `data/` into `IDPForge/data/`.

```bash
# After downloading and extracting from Figshare
cp -r weights/ /path/to/IDPForge/weights/
cp -r data/* /path/to/IDPForge/data/
```

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L200-L204)

### Alternative: HPC / OpenFold-Led Installation

If the direct `environment.yml` approach fails (common on tightly managed clusters), install via the OpenFold-led path instead. Clone both repos side-by-side, strip `flash-attn` from OpenFold's environment file, create the env with `mamba`, then add IDPForge's missing dependencies manually:

```bash
conda install einops mdtraj pdb-tools -c conda-forge
conda install mmseqs2 -c bioconda
pip install tensorboard topoly
```

Then install both packages with `pip install . --no-build-isolation` (fall back to `pip install -e .` if that fails). See [Docker and HPC Setup](3-docker-and-hpc-setup) for containerized alternatives.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L99-L198)

## Your First IDP Ensemble

Once the environment is active and weights are in place, generating an ensemble is a single command. IDPForge ships two sampling modes depending on your target:

| Mode | Script | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| **Fully disordered** | `sample_idp.py` | Single-chain intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) |
| **Partially disordered** | `sample_ldr.py` | Proteins with folded domains + intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) |

### Sampling a Fully Disordered Protein (IDP)

The `sample_idp.py` script takes a protein sequence directly on the command line. Here we generate **10 conformers** for yeast Sic1, a well-studied IDP:

```bash
mkdir test
sequence="GSMTPSTPPRSRGTRYLAQPSGNTSSSALMQGQKTPQKPSQNLVPVTPSTTKSFKNAPLLAPPNSNMGMTSPFNGLTSPQRSPFPKSSVKRT"
python sample_idp.py $sequence weights/mdl.ckpt test configs/sample.yml \
    --nconf 10 --batch 4 --cuda --verbose
```

The positional and optional arguments are:

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `seq` | Yes | Amino acid sequence (one-letter code) |
| `ckpt_path` | Yes | Path to model checkpoint (e.g. `weights/mdl.ckpt`) |
| `output_dir` | Yes | Directory for output PDB files |
| `sample_cfg` | Yes | Path to sampling config YAML |
| `--batch` | No | Batch size per diffusion round (default: 32) |
| `--nconf` | No | Total conformers to generate (default: 100) |
| `--cuda` | No | Use GPU acceleration |
| `--verbose` | No | Print structural validation details |

Each conformer passes through a three-phase pipeline automatically: **Generate + Relax** (AMBER minimization), **Repair** (chirality + HIS ring fixes), and **Validate** (bond integrity, clash score, knot detection). Passing structures are saved as `N_validated.pdb`.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L282-L319), [sample_idp.py](/sample_idp.py#L172-L193)

### Sampling a Protein with Folded Domains (IDR)

For proteins that contain both structured and disordered regions, first **prepare the folded template**, then sample:

**Step A — Create the template** from an AlphaFold DB PDB, specifying the disordered residue range:

```bash
python mk_ldr_template.py data/AF-P05231-F1-model_v4.pdb 1-41 data/AF-P05231_ndr.npz
```

This writes an `.npz` file containing the folded-domain coordinates, torsion angles, and disorder mask that the sampler uses as a fixed scaffold.

**Step B — Sample the IDR ensemble** around that template:

```bash
mkdir P05231_build
python sample_ldr.py weights/mdl.ckpt data/AF-P05231_ndr.npz P05231_build configs/sample.yml \
    --nconf 10 --batch 4 --cuda --verbose
```

For long sequences, manage GPU memory with `--attention_chunk` (lower = less memory, slower). The provided model weights are **not recommended for predicting multiple disordered domains simultaneously** — use the AlphaFlex pipeline for multi-domain cases.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L336-L361), [mk_ldr_template.py](/mk_ldr_template.py#L1-L26), [sample_ldr.py](/sample_ldr.py#L233-L292)

## Configuration at a Glance

Sampling behavior is controlled by `configs/sample.yml`. The key sections you will interact with most:

| Section | Key Parameters | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `diffuse` | `n_tsteps: 200`, `inference_steps: 40` | Diffusion schedule: total timesteps and denoising steps |
| `potential` | `false` / `potential_cfg` | Enable experimental guidance (PRE, NOE, Rg) |
| `relax` | `stiffness: 10.0`, `max_outer_iterations: 20` | AMBER relaxation strength and iterations |
| `model` | `trunk.*`, `structure_module.*` | Transformer architecture (normally left at defaults) |

To **activate experimental guidance**, set `potential: true` and configure the `potential_cfg` block. For example, PRE data for Sic1 is provided at `data/sic1_pre_exp.txt`:

```yaml
potential: true
potential_cfg:
  pre:
    exp_path: data/sic1_pre_exp.txt
    exp_mask_p: 0.8
  timescale: 10
  grad_clip: 0.1
```

Sources: [configs/sample.yml](/configs/sample.yml#L1-L57)

## Training (Optional)

To train IDPForge on your own data, prepare a training pickle (see `data/README.md` for the format) and run:

```bash
python train.py --model_config_path configs/train.yml
```

Training uses PyTorch Lightning and is customizable via the `trainer` section in `configs/train.yml` (learning rate, gradient clipping, accumulation, epochs, etc.). The training config mirrors the sampling config's model architecture but adds loss weights, an EMA decay, and a OneCycleLR scheduler.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L273-L279), [train.py](/train.py#L122-L155), [configs/train.yml](/configs/train.yml#L1-L94)

## Quick-Reference Command Summary

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| **IDP sampling** | `python sample_idp.py SEQ weights/mdl.ckpt OUTDIR configs/sample.yml --nconf N --cuda` |
| **Template creation** | `python mk_ldr_template.py PDB RANGE output.npz` |
| **IDR sampling** | `python sample_ldr.py weights/mdl.ckpt TEMPLATE.npz OUTDIR configs/sample.yml --nconf N --cuda` |
| **Training** | `python train.py --model_config_path configs/train.yml` |
| **Ensemble scoring** | `python score_ensemble.py PROTEIN ENSDIR --jc --noe --pre --fret` |

> [!TIP]
> All sampling scripts automatically resume from existing `*_validated.pdb` files in the output directory — simply re-run the same command to continue generating conformers toward your target `--nconf` count.

- **Deploy on clusters**: [Docker and HPC Setup](3-docker-and-hpc-setup)

# Docker and HPC Setup



IDPForge ships **three deployment formats** — Docker images, Apptainer (Singularity) definition files, and a bare Conda environment — each available in **two GPU-architecture variants**: Ampere (CUDA 12.1) and Blackwell (CUDA 12.8). This page walks you through selecting the right variant, building the container or environment, and running your first sampling job inside it. The build pipeline is deliberately uniform across formats: every path shares the same Conda dependency manifest, the same pip pin, and the same OpenFold CUDA-extension patch — the only axis of variation is the CUDA/PyTorch version pair matched to your hardware.

## GPU Architecture Variants

The two variants exist because OpenFold's custom CUDA kernel (`attn_core_inplace_cuda`) must be compiled against compute capabilities that match the target GPU. IDPForge patches OpenFold's `setup.py` to control exactly which `sm_*` codes are emitted during the build.

| Variant | CUDA Toolkit | PyTorch | Compute Capabilities | Target GPUs |
|---------|-------------|---------|---------------------|-------------|
| **Ampere** | 12.1 | 2.5.1 | sm_61 (Pascal), sm_70 (Volta), sm_80 (Ampere) | A40, A100, V100, T4, GTX 1080+ |
| **Blackwell** | 12.8 | 2.7.1 | sm_61–sm_80 + sm_90 (Hopper/Ada), sm_120 (Blackwell) | H100, B200, RTX 5090, L40S |

The OpenFold setup patches make this distinction concrete. The Ampere variant compiles for three architectures:

```python
compute_capabilities = set([
    (6, 1), # Pascal
    (7, 0), # Volta
    (8, 0), # Ampere (A40/A100)
])
```

While the Blackwell variant extends the set with Hopper and Blackwell codes:

```python
compute_capabilities = set([
    (6, 1),  # Pascal
    (7, 0),  # Volta
    (8, 0),  # Ampere (A40/A100)
    (9, 0),  # Hopper/Ada
    (12, 0), # Blackwell
])
```

> [!TIP]
> Choose the **Ampere** variant if your HPC cluster runs NVIDIA A100/A40 or older GPUs — it is the safer default. Use **Blackwell** only when you know the target machine has Hopper (sm_90) or Blackwell (sm_120) hardware; the additional compute-capability flags increase compilation time and image size.

Sources: [openfold_setup_12.1.py](dockerfiles/openfold_setup_12.1.py#L55-L61), [openfold_setup_12.8.py](dockerfiles/openfold_setup_12.8.py#L55-L65)

## Docker Deployment

### Build

From the repository root, build the image matching your GPU architecture:

```bash
# Ampere variant (most clusters)
docker build -f dockerfiles/Dockerfile_Ampere -t idpforge:ampere .

# Blackwell variant (H100 / B200 clusters)
docker build -f dockerfiles/Dockerfile_Blackwell -t idpforge:blackwell .
```

Both Dockerfiles follow an identical layered construction strategy, differing only in the base image tag and PyTorch wheel index. The build pipeline proceeds through these stages:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["nvidia/cuda base image"] --> B["System packages\n(wget, git, build-essential)"]
    B --> C["Miniforge + mamba"]
    D["Conda env from env.yml\n(CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA=12.2)"]
    C --> D
    D --> E["Pin pip==25.2"]
    E --> F["PyTorch + DeepSpeed"]
    F --> G["OpenFold\n(patched setup.py + CUDA ext)"]
    G --> H["IDPForge source\ncopy + PYTHONPATH"]
    H --> I["Build-time\nimport self-test"]
```

### Run

Invoke sampling with GPU passthrough. The `--gpus all` flag is required for CUDA access inside the container:

```bash
docker run --gpus all -v $(pwd)/out:/app/out idpforge:ampere \
    python sample_idp.py \
    "MVKETFYTVGD" ./weights/mdl.ckpt /app/out \
    ./configs/sample.yml --nconf 10 --cuda --verbose
```

For ensemble scoring, mount experimental data as an additional volume:

```bash
docker run --gpus all \
    -v $(pwd)/out:/app/out \
    -v $(pwd)/exp_data:/data \
    -e IDPFORGE_EXP_DATA=/data \
    idpforge:ampere \
    python score_ensemble.py asyn /app/out --jc --noe --pre --fret
```

> [!TIP]
> The `CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA=12.2` environment variable is set during the Conda env creation step. This is critical because Docker builds execute on the CPU — without it, Conda would resolve the **CPU-only** variant of OpenMM, which cannot perform GPU-accelerated AMBER relaxation at runtime.

Sources: [Dockerfile_Ampere](dockerfiles/Dockerfile_Ampere#L1-L64), [Dockerfile_Blackwell](dockerfiles/Dockerfile_Blackwell#L1-L64)

## Apptainer (Singularity) Deployment for HPC

HPC clusters typically restrict Docker but allow Apptainer/Singularity containers. IDPForge provides `.def` definition files that build SIF images from the same NVIDIA CUDA base, using Apptainer's fakeroot build mode.

### Build

```bash
# Ampere variant
apptainer build idpforge_ampere.sif dockerfiles/idpforge_ampere.def

# Blackwell variant
apptainer build idpforge_blackwell.sif dockerfiles/idpforge_blackwell.def
```

> **Prerequisites before building**: You must have the model checkpoint (`weights/mdl.ckpt`) and fragment library (`data/example_data.pkl`) present in the repository tree — the `%files` section copies the `weights/` and `data/` directories into the image at `/opt/IDPForge/`.

### Run

The `--nv` flag binds the host's NVIDIA driver and CUDA libraries into the container. Bind-mount the output directory so sampled structures persist on the host filesystem:

```bash
# Sampling
apptainer run --nv --pwd /opt/IDPForge \
    -B "$PWD/out":/app/out \
    idpforge_ampere.sif /opt/IDPForge/sample_idp.py \
        "MVKETFYTVGD" /opt/IDPForge/weights/mdl.ckpt /app/out \
        /opt/IDPForge/configs/sample.yml --nconf 10 --cuda --verbose
```

```bash
# Scoring (experimental data not bundled — mount separately)
apptainer run --nv \
    -B "$PWD/../Data/exp":/data \
    --env IDPFORGE_EXP_DATA=/data \
    idpforge_ampere.sif /opt/IDPForge/score_ensemble.py \
        asyn /app/out --jc --noe --pre --fret
```

### Apptainer vs Docker: Structural Differences

| Aspect | Docker | Apptainer |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| Source inclusion | `COPY . /app` (full tree) | `%files` — explicit per-directory copy to `/opt/IDPForge/` |
| Python path | `ENV PYTHONPATH="/app"` | `%environment` exports `PYTHONPATH=/opt/IDPForge` |
| Entrypoint | None (explicit `python` in `docker run`) | `%runscript exec python "$@"` — script path is the sole argument |
| GPU access | `--gpus all` (Docker runtime) | `--nv` (host driver bind) |
| Self-test | `RUN python - <<'PY' ...` (fail-fast at build) | `%test` block (run via `apptainer test`) |
| Locale config | Not set | `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`, `LANG=C.UTF-8` |
| Build user | Root | Fakeroot (Apptainer default) |

Sources: [idpforge_ampere.def](dockerfiles/idpforge_ampere.def#L1-L121), [idpforge_blackwell.def](dockerfiles/idpforge_blackwell.def#L1-L121)

## Conda Environment (Bare Metal)

If you prefer a native Conda installation — for example, on a workstation with a supported NVIDIA driver — use the root-level `environment.yml`. It contains inline comments marking the four lines you must toggle when switching from the Ampere default to the Blackwell alternative.

### Setup

```bash
# Create the environment (Ampere default)
mamba env create -f environment.yml
conda activate IDPForge

# Install IDPForge as an editable package
pip install -e .
```

### Switching to the Blackwell Variant

Edit `environment.yml` and change the **four marked lines**:

| Line | Default (Ampere) | Alternative (Blackwell) |
|------|-------------------|------------------------|
| `cuda-toolkit` | `nvidia::cuda-toolkit=12.1` | `nvidia::cuda-toolkit=12.8` |
| `cuda-version` | `conda-forge::cuda-version=12.1` | `conda-forge::cuda-version=12.8` |
| `--extra-index-url` | `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121` | `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128` |
| `torch` | `torch==2.5.1` | `torch==2.7.1` |

After editing, recreate the environment:

```bash
mamba env remove -n IDPForge
mamba env create -f environment.yml
conda activate IDPForge
pip install -e .
```

Sources: [environment.yml](environment.yml#L1-L82)

## Shared Dependency Manifest

Both the Docker and Apptainer builds consume `dockerfiles/env.yml` as their Conda dependency source. This manifest is a focused subset of the root `environment.yml` — it omits `cuda-toolkit` (supplied by the base image) and `gcc` (supplied by the devel image's system packages), delegating those to the container layer. The key dependency groups are:

| Group | Packages | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| Scientific & MD | `openmm`, `pdbfixer`, `mdtraj`, `biopython`, `scipy` | AMBER relaxation, structure I/O, trajectory analysis |
| Bioinformatics | `hmmer`, `hhsuite`, `kalign2`, `mmseqs2` | MSA generation for OpenFold |
| ML Core | `torch`, `pytorch-lightning`, `deepspeed` | Diffusion model training & inference |
| Data & Logging | `numpy`, `pandas`, `tensorboard`, `wandb` | Experiment tracking, data wrangling |
| Utilities | `PyYAML`, `tqdm`, `einops`, `ml-collections`, `aria2` | Config parsing, progress, tensor reshaping, downloads |

A **strict pip pin at version 25.2** is enforced in all three deployment formats. The Dockerfiles and `.def` files assert this invariant after every `pip install` call:

```bash
pip install --no-deps "pip==25.2" && \
    test "$(pip --version | awk '{print $2}')" = "25.2"
```

This ensures that no downstream dependency silently upgrades pip to a version that breaks IDPForge's installation graph.

Sources: [env.yml](dockerfiles/env.yml#L1-L51), [Dockerfile_Ampere](dockerfiles/Dockerfile_Ampere#L30-L32)

## Build-Time Verification

All container images embed a **self-test** that runs at the end of the build. It imports every critical package and prints the PyTorch/CUDA version pair, causing the build to fail immediately if any dependency is missing or misconfigured:

```python
import torch, numpy, scipy, pandas, mdtraj, yaml, tqdm
import ml_collections, einops
import Bio.PDB
import openmm, pdbfixer
import pytorch_lightning, tensorboard, modelcif
import openfold, idpforge, esm
print("torch:", torch.__version__, "cuda build:", torch.version.cuda)
print("idpforge ok, openfold ok, esm ok")
```

In Docker, this executes as a `RUN` step — a failed import **fails the build**. In Apptainer, it lives in the `%test` section and can be invoked post-hoc with `apptainer test idpforge.sif`.

Sources: [Dockerfile_Ampere](dockerfiles/Dockerfile_Ampere#L58-L64), [idpforge_ampere.def](dockerfiles/idpforge_ampere.def#L107-L115)

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `openmm` imports but runs on CPU | `CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA` not set during build | Rebuild — the env.yml step must run with `CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA=12.2` |
| OpenFold CUDA extension fails to compile | Wrong compute capabilities for your GPU | Verify GPU arch with `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=compute_cap --format=csv` and select matching variant |
| `pip` version mismatch breaks installs | A downstream package upgraded pip past 25.2 | Re-pin: `pip install --no-deps "pip==25.2"` |
| Apptainer build fails in `%post` | Fakeroot cannot write to `/opt` | Use `apptainer build --fakeroot` or run as root on a build node |
| `ImportError: No module named 'idpforge'` at runtime | `PYTHONPATH` not exported in container | Docker: check `ENV PYTHONPATH`; Apptainer: verify `%environment` block |
| `--cs` scoring flag has no effect | CSpred external tool is not bundled | Install CSpred on the host and mount it into the container |

## Where to Go Next

Once your environment is operational, proceed to the core workflow pages:

- **[Architecture Overview](4-architecture-overview)** — understand how the components you just installed interact at runtime
- **[IDP Sampling (Fully Disordered)](12-idp-sampling-fully-disordered)** — run your first end-to-end sampling job with the container you just built
- **[Configuration Reference](22-configuration-reference)** — tune the `sample.yml` and `train.yml` configs for your hardware and sequence

# Architecture Overview



IDPForge is a **transformer protein language diffusion model** that generates all-atom structural ensembles for intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) that maintain their folded domains. The system couples a modified ESMFold trunk with a three-factor diffusion process operating over SE(3) backbone frames, SO(3) rotational components, and torsion angle space — then closes the loop with experimental guidance potentials, AMBER relaxation, and X-EISD ensemble scoring.

## System Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph Training["Training Pipeline"]
        TL[IDPloader<br/>Data + Diffusion] --> TW[IDPForgeWrapper<br/>Lightning + EMA]
        TW --> TM[IDPForge Model]
        TM --> TF[FoldingTrunk<br/>ESMFold Transformer]
        TL -->|noised batch| TW
        TW -->|loss signals| TL
    end

    subgraph Diffusion["Three-Factor Diffusion Engine"]
        D[Diffuser] --> D1[EuclideanDiffuser<br/>Cα translations]
        D --> D2[IGSO3<br/>Backbone rotations]
        D --> D3[TorsionDiffuser<br/>Sidechain χ angles]
        DN[Denoiser] --> D
        DN --> GNP[get_next_pose<br/>Reverse step]
        GNP --> GCA[get_next_ca]
        GNP --> GF[get_next_frames]
        GNP --> GT[get_next_chi_angles]
    end

    subgraph Inference["Sampling & Inference"]
        SIDP[sample_idp.py<br/>Full IDP] --> DN
        SLDR[sample_ldr.py<br/>IDR + Template] --> DN
        DN --> RECON[model.recon<br/>Reverse diffusion loop]
        RECON --> POT[Potential Gradients<br/>Experimental Guidance]
    end

    subgraph PostProc["Post-Processing"]
        POT --> PR[Pre-Relax Screening]
        PR --> RLX[AMBER Relaxation<br/>+ Repair]
        RLX --> SV[Structure Validation]
        SV --> XE[X-EISD Ensemble Scoring]
    end

    TW -.->|EMA weights| RECON
    D -.->|Forward noising| TL
```

The architecture divides into four principal subsystems: **(1)** a training pipeline that jointly noises ground-truth structures and trains the denoising network, **(2)** a diffusion engine providing forward noising and reverse denoising across three geometric factors, **(3)** an inference subsystem supporting both fully disordered and template-conditioned sampling with experimental potentials, and **(4)** a post-processing chain that screens, relaxes, validates, and scores the resulting conformers.

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L1-L283), [wrapper.py](/idpforge/wrapper.py#L1-L208), [diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L1-L685)

## Core Model: IDPForge Transformer

The `IDPForge` module is the neural denoising network. It extends the ESMFold `FoldingTrunk` with diffusion-specific input conditioning — transforming a noised structure at timestep *t* into a predicted clean structure. The model ingests four input streams: **sinusoidal timestep embeddings**, **noised torsion angle features** (α_t), **amino acid identity embeddings**, and **secondary structure type embeddings**. These are fused into a per-residue single state vector *s_s* that, together with a pairwise state *s_z* derived from noised backbone geometry, feeds the FoldingTrunk's attention-based structure prediction pipeline.

| Component | Input | Output | Dimensionality |
|---|---|---|---|
| `time_embed` | Timestep index *t* | Sinusoidal embedding | → `t_embed_dim` (32) |
| `esm_s_mlp` | [time_embed ⊕ α_t] | Single-state *s_s* | → `c_s` (384) |
| `z_mlp` | Pairwise distance bins | Pairwise-state *s_z* | → `c_z` (128) |
| `aa_embedding` | Residue type | Additive to *s_s* | → `c_s` |
| `ss_embedding` | SS type (H/E/C/…) | Additive to *s_s* | → `c_s` |
| `FoldingTrunk` | *s_s*, *s_z*, sequence | Frames, angles, positions | SE(3) + torsion output |

The forward pass supports **self-conditioning** via recycle: predictions from the previous iteration's output are injected as additional bias terms through `recycle_s_norm`, `recycle_z_norm`, and `recycle_disto`, enabling iterative refinement within a single denoising step. The `recon` method implements the full reverse diffusion loop, stepping from *t = T* down to *t = 0* while optionally fixing template residues at their native coordinates.

> [!TIP]
> The secondary structure embedding is randomly dropped to all-coil (sstype=7) with 20% probability during training, which teaches the model to generate disordered conformations even without explicit SS guidance — critical for IDP ensemble diversity.

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L30-L120), [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L122-L200), [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L202-L283)

## Three-Factor Diffusion Engine

IDPForge decomposes protein structure diffusion into three independent geometric channels, each with its own noise schedule and reverse-step algorithm. This factorization mirrors the natural symmetries of protein backbone geometry: translations live in ℝ³, backbone rotations in SO(3), and sidechain conformations in the torsion angle torus.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Forward["Forward Noising (Diffuser)"]
        A[Clean Structure] --> B1["EuclideanDiffuser<br/>β schedule on Cα"]
        A --> B2["IGSO3<br/>σ schedule on frames"]
        A --> B3["TorsionDiffuser<br/>β schedule on χ"]
        B1 --> C["Noised x_t, R_t, α_t"]
        B2 --> C
        B3 --> C
    end

    subgraph Reverse["Reverse Denoising (Denoiser)"]
        C --> D1["get_next_ca<br/>Gaussian posterior"]
        C --> D2["get_next_frames<br/>IGSO3 score sampling"]
        C --> D3["get_next_chi_angles<br/>Wrapped Gaussian"]
        D1 --> E["Updated x_{t-1}, α_{t-1}"]
        D2 --> E
        D3 --> E
    end
```

**Euclidean Cα Diffusion** applies a variance-preserving schedule with linear β from `euclid_b0` to `euclid_bT`. The reverse step computes the Gaussian posterior mean μ(x_t, x̂_0) and variance σ² using the standard DDPM derivation, then adds scaled noise to produce x_{t-1}. All backbone atoms (N, Cα, C, O, Cβ) are translated by the same δ per residue.

**IGSO(3) Frame Diffusion** operates on rotation matrices derived from backbone triplets (N-Cα-C). The forward pass samples rotation vectors from the IGSO(3) distribution using precomputed CDFs. The reverse step computes a score approximation from the predicted R_0 and current R_t, then combines this with stochastic noise scaled by the drift coefficient g(t). This is adapted from the RFdiffusion SO(3) framework.

**Torsion Angle Diffusion** applies the same variance-preserving schedule to sidechain χ angles, with wrapping to [-π, π) to respect the circular topology. A `torsion_mask` ensures that only residues with valid χ angles (e.g., not alanine or glycine) are diffused.

| Diffusion Channel | Space | Schedule | Reverse Method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cα Translations | ℝ³ | Linear β (DDPM) | Gaussian posterior + noise |
| Backbone Rotations | SO(3) | Quadratic σ (IGSO3) | Score-based SDE discretization |
| Torsion Angles | [-π, π)⁴ | Linear β (wrapped) | Wrapped Gaussian posterior |

Sources: [diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L1-L200), [diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L200-L400), [diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L400-L685)

## Training Pipeline

The training loop is orchestrated by `IDPForgeWrapper`, a PyTorch Lightning module that manages the interaction between the model, the diffuser, the data loader, and the loss computation. During each training step, a random timestep *T* is sampled with linearly increasing weights (favoring later, noisier timesteps), and the model is trained to predict the clean structure from the noised snapshot at that timestep.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant DL as IDPloader
    participant TW as IDPForgeWrapper
    participant DF as Diffuser
    participant M as IDPForge
    participant L as Loss Functions

    DL->>DF: diffuse_pose(coords, seq)
    DF-->>DL: "{x_t, R_t, α_t} for all T"
    DL->>TW: "batch with noised data at random T"
    TW->>M: "forward(t, α_t, x_t, batch)"
    M-->>TW: "predicted {frames, angles, positions}"
    TW->>L: "calc_loss(pred, true_rigids, true_coords, true_torsions)"
    L-->>TW: "weighted loss sum"
    TW->>TW: "EMA update on_before_zero_grad"
```

The **data pipeline** (`IDPloader` → `DiffDataset` → `BatchCollator`) pre-computes the full forward diffusion trajectory for each training structure at setup time. Each `__getitem__` call selects a random timestep and returns the noised snapshot at both *t* and *t+1* (the latter for self-conditioning). The `BatchCollator` handles variable-length sequences through padding and dense tensor collation.

The **loss function** combines four complementary terms: **FAPE** (Frame Aligned Point Error) measuring backbone and sidechain rigidity alignment, **angular loss** on predicted vs. true torsion angles, **violation loss** penalizing steric clashes and bond geometry deviations, and **Cβ distance loss** enforcing inter-residue distance agreement with special treatment for secondary structure regions.

Sources: [wrapper.py](/idpforge/wrapper.py#L1-L208), [loader.py](/idpforge/loader.py#L1-L145), [loss.py](/idpforge/loss.py#L1-L189)

## Sampling and Inference

IDPForge provides two sampling modes that share the same reverse diffusion engine but differ in how template constraints and initial conditions are handled.

**Full IDP Sampling** (`sample_idp.py`) generates conformational ensembles for completely disordered proteins. Each conformer begins from isotropic Gaussian noise in translation, IGSO(3)-sampled rotations, and uniform torsion angles. Secondary structure assignments are sampled from a pre-built SS database matched by sequence, with random selection per conformer to capture structural diversity. The generation loop runs until the requested number of validated conformers is reached, with automatic resume via file counting.

**IDR Sampling with Folded Template** (`sample_ldr.py`) generates disordered regions while preserving a folded structural template. Template residues have their timesteps forced to *t = 0* and their coordinates/torsions fixed at native values throughout reverse diffusion, so the denoiser only updates the IDR positions. The template `.npz` file provides the sequence, folded coordinates, secondary structure, a binary mask, and torsion angles. For large templates, a truncation mechanism emits a `_truncation.json` graft specification for downstream reassembly via the AlphaFlex stitching pipeline.

| Feature | IDP Sampling | IDR Sampling |
|---|---|---|
| Initial state | Isotropic noise | Noise for IDR; native for fold |
| Template constraint | None | Fixed coordinates at t=0 |
| SS source | Database lookup | Hybrid (fold SS + IDR SS) |
| Typical use case | Fully disordered proteins | Partially structured proteins |
| Script | `sample_idp.py` | `sample_ldr.py` |

Sources: [sample_idp.py](/sample_idp.py#L1-L194), [sample_ldr.py](/sample_ldr.py#L1-L200), [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L202-L283)

## Experimental Guidance Potentials

During reverse diffusion, differentiable potential functions bias the denoising trajectory toward agreement with experimental data. Each potential computes a scalar energy from the current predicted structure, and its gradient (computed via autograd) is added to the predicted x̂_0 before the reverse step. The `Potential` base class defines the interface; concrete implementations include:

| Potential | Experimental Data | Computation |
|---|---|---|
| `RoG` | Ensemble-averaged Rg | (Rg_pred − Rg_target)² |
| `Contact` | PRE / NOE distances | Switched inverse-distance matching |
| `Efret` | FRET efficiencies | Förster resonance transfer model |
| `JCoup` | J-coupling constants | Karplus equation on backbone φ |

The `Multiple` potential allows weighted combination of any of the above. Potentials are controlled by a timescale parameter (determining when during diffusion they become active) and a gradient clipping threshold to prevent instability. The gradient is applied only to Cα positions and broadcast to all backbone atoms.

Sources: [potential.py](/idpforge/utils/potential.py#L1-L170)

## Post-Processing Chain

Every generated conformer passes through a multi-stage validation and refinement pipeline before being accepted into the final ensemble.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    RAW[Raw Diffusion Output] --> PR[Pre-Relax Screening<br/>CA continuity check]
    PR -->|pass| RLX[AMBER Relaxation<br/>Position restraints on fold]
    PR -->|fail| REJ[Reject]
    RLX --> SV[Structure Validation<br/>Chirality + Bonds + Clashes + Knots]
    SV -->|pass| VALID[Validated PDB]
    SV -->|fail| REJ
    VALID --> XE[X-EISD Scoring<br/>Ensemble selection]
```

**Pre-Relax Screening** checks consecutive Cα-Cα distances before any expensive relaxation. Junction residues (at fold-IDR boundaries) use a more permissive threshold (6.46 Å) than interior backbone bonds (9.12 Å). This filters catastrophically broken conformers early.

**AMBER Relaxation** applies OpenMM-based energy minimization with positional restraints on folded domain residues (excluding IDR residues from restraint). The `structure_repair` module handles common artifacts like flipped chirality and broken bonds before minimization.

**Structure Validation** performs comprehensive checks: chirality (D-amino acid detection via triple product), bond integrity (heavy-atom graph comparison against canonical connectivity), steric clashes (VDW overlap via KD-tree), and knot topology (Alexander polynomial screening with AlphaKnot2 hybrid detection). Knot expectations can be specified per-domain via a JSON screening file.

**X-EISD Ensemble Scoring** computes maximum log-likelihood scores for the ensemble against experimental data (chemical shifts, J-couplings, PRE/NOE distances, FRET). Each property uses property-specific back-calculators and optimal parameter estimation to compute a log-likelihood, and the total score determines the optimal ensemble subset.

Sources: [pre_relax.py](/idpforge/utils/pre_relax.py#L1-L30), [structure_validation.py](/idpforge/utils/structure_validation.py#L1-L200), [scorer.py](/scoring/scorer.py#L1-L136)

## ESM2 Integration

The `ESM_preprocess` module wraps Meta's ESM2 protein language model to compute per-residue embeddings and optional attention maps. It supports the full ESM2 model family (8M through 15B parameters). During template-based data preparation (`mk_flex_template.py`, `mk_ldr_template.py`), ESM2 embeddings can be pre-computed and cached, avoiding redundant inference during training. The wrapper maps AlphaFold2 residue indices to ESM token indices, adds BOS/EOS tokens, and extracts intermediate layer representations.

Sources: [esm_wrapper.py](/idpforge/esm_wrapper.py#L1-L100)

## Module Organization

```
idpforge/                        # Core library
├── model.py                     # IDPForge transformer (denoising network)
├── wrapper.py                   # PyTorch Lightning training wrapper + EMA
├── loader.py                    # DiffDataset + IDPloader (noised data pipeline)
├── loss.py                      # Multi-component loss (FAPE, angular, violation, dist)
├── misc.py                      # I/O: PDB writing, SS encoding, input processing
├── esm_wrapper.py               # ESM2 embedding pre-computation
└── utils/
    ├── diff_utils.py            # Diffuser + Denoiser + 3-factor diffusion
    ├── igso3_utils.py           # IGSO(3) distribution computation
    ├── potential.py             # Experimental guidance potentials
    ├── pre_relax.py             # Pre-relaxation backbone screening
    ├── relax.py                 # AMBER relaxation via OpenMM
    ├── structure_repair.py      # Chirality/bond repair before relaxation
    ├── structure_validation.py  # Comprehensive conformer validation
    └── validation_metrics.py    # Rg and other ensemble metrics

scoring/                         # X-EISD ensemble scoring
├── scorer.py                    # Per-property log-likelihood scoring
├── calculator.py                # Back-calculator orchestration
├── optimizer.py                 # Ensemble subset optimization
└── normalize.py                 # Score normalization

AlphaFlex/                       # AlphaFold + IDPForge hybrid pipeline
├── Step_1_case_label.py         # IDR classification from AF2 structures
├── Step_1B_subset_label.py      # Subset re-labeling
├── Step_2_mk_ldr_template.py   # Template creation for IDR sampling
├── Step_3_sample_conformer.py   # Conformer generation (calls sample_ldr)
├── Step_4_ldr_stitch.py         # Monte Carlo stitching of truncated domains
└── utils/
    ├── stitch.py                # MC assembly logic
    ├── graft_back.py            # Grafting folded domains back
    └── smart_scoring.py         # Integrated scoring for stitching
```

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L1-L283), [wrapper.py](/idpforge/wrapper.py#L1-L208), [diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L1-L685), [loss.py](/idpforge/loss.py#L1-L189)

## Where to Go Next

The architecture overview establishes the system-level picture. To understand each subsystem in depth, follow this progression:

1. **Core Model** — Start with [IDPForge Transformer Network](5-idpforge-transformer-network) for the denoising network internals, then [SE(3) Backbone Diffusion](6-se-3-backbone-diffusion) and [SO(3) Rotational Diffusion](7-so-3-rotational-diffusion) for the geometric diffusion machinery, and [Torsion Angle Diffusion](8-torsion-angle-diffusion) for sidechain modeling.
2. **Training** — See [Training Workflow and Configuration](9-training-workflow-and-configuration) and [Loss Functions](10-loss-functions) for the optimization setup.
3. **Inference** — [IDP Sampling (Fully Disordered)](12-idp-sampling-fully-disordered) and [IDR Sampling with Folded Templates](13-idr-sampling-with-folded-templates) cover the two sampling modes; [Experimental Guidance Potentials](14-experimental-guidance-potentials) explains how NMR/FRET data steer generation.
4. **Quality Control** — [AMBER Relaxation and Repair](15-amber-relaxation-and-repair), [Structure Validation Pipeline](16-structure-validation-pipeline), and [X-EISD Ensemble Scoring](17-x-eisd-ensemble-scoring) detail the post-processing chain.
5. **Hybrid Pipeline** — [AlphaFlex Workflow Overview](18-alphaflex-workflow-overview) and [Monte Carlo Stitching and Assembly](20-monte-carlo-stitching-and-assembly) cover the end-to-end workflow for partially structured proteins.

# IDPForge Transformer Network



The IDPForge Transformer Network is the core neural architecture that drives structure prediction within a diffusion framework. It extends the ESMFold trunk with diffusion-timestep conditioning, noised-coordinate pairwise featurization, and secondary-structure embeddings — transforming a single-shot structure predictor into a **denoising network** capable of iteratively refining intrinsically disordered protein conformations from noise.

## Architectural Overview

The network follows a **dual-track transformer** paradigm: a sequence-state track (per-residue) and a pairwise-state track (residue-pair) exchange information through coupled attention blocks, culminating in an Invariant Point Attention (IPA) structure module. What distinguishes IDPForge from the base ESMFold trunk is the **diffusion-aware input featurization** that injects timestep, torsion, and noised-geometry signals into the initial hidden states.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Inputs
        T["t<br/>(timestep index)"]
        AT["α_t<br/>(torsion features)"]
        XT["x_t<br/>(noised coords)"]
        AA["aa<br/>(amino acid)"]
        SS["ss<br/>(secondary structure)"]
    end

    subgraph Featurization["Input Featurization"]
        TSINE["Sinusoidal Embed<br/>(frozen)"]
        SMLP["esm_s_mlp<br/>LayerNorm→Linear→ReLU→Linear"]
        AAEMB["aa_embedding"]
        SSEMB["ss_embedding"]
        T2D["xyz_to_t2d<br/>(dist + orient + RBF)"]
        ZMLP["z_mlp<br/>LayerNorm→Linear→ReLU→Linear"]
    end

    T --> TSINE
    TSINE --> SMLP
    AT --> SMLP
    SMLP --> SS0["s_s₀"]
    AA --> AAEMB
    AAEMB --> SS0
    SS --> SSEMB
    SSEMB --> SS0

    XT --> T2D
    AA --> T2D
    T2D --> ZMLP
    ZMLP --> SZ0["s_z₀"]

    subgraph Trunk["FoldingTrunk (N blocks + recycling)"]
        RPE["RelativePosition<br/>Embedding"]
        TAB["TriangularSelfAttention<br/>Block × N"]
        SM["StructureModule<br/>(IPA)"]
        RCE["Recycle<br/>Feedback"]
    end

    SS0 --> Trunk
    SZ0 --> Trunk
    RCE -.-> Trunk

    Trunk --> OUT["{frames, angles,<br/>positions, s_s, s_z}"]

    style Featurization fill:#e8f4fd,stroke:#2980b9
    style Trunk fill:#fef9e7,stroke:#f39c12
    style Inputs fill:#fde8e8,stroke:#e74c3c
```

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L36-L153), [trunk.py](/esm/esmfold/trunk.py#L113-L227)

## The IDPForge Module

The `IDPForge` class is the top-level `nn.Module` that orchestrates featurization and delegates to the `FoldingTrunk`. Its constructor receives two critical diffusion parameters — `n_tsteps` (total training timesteps) and `inf_tsteps` (inference sub-steps) — alongside an `IDPConfig` dataclass that controls every architectural dimension.

### Configuration Dataclass

| Parameter | Default | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `t_embed_dim` | 32 | Dimensionality of sinusoidal timestep embedding |
| `trunk` | `FoldingTrunkConfig()` | Nested config for the FoldingTrunk (blocks, dims, recycling) |

The `FoldingTrunkConfig` in turn exposes the dimensions that define the transformer's capacity:

| Parameter | Default | Training Config | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `num_blocks` | 48 | 2 | Number of TriangularSelfAttention blocks |
| `sequence_state_dim` | 1024 | 128 | Per-residue hidden dimension (c_s) |
| `pairwise_state_dim` | 128 | 64 | Per-pair hidden dimension (c_z) |
| `sequence_head_width` | 32 | 32 | Width per attention head (sequence track) |
| `pairwise_head_width` | 32 | 32 | Width per attention head (pairwise track) |
| `max_recycles` | 3 | 3 | Recycling iterations during inference |
| `structure_module.c_s` | 384 | 256 | Structure module single state dim |
| `structure_module.c_z` | 128 | 64 | Structure module pair state dim |
| `structure_module.no_blocks` | 8 | 4 | IPA structure module layers |

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L30-L33), [trunk.py](/esm/esmfold/trunk.py#L17-L54), [train.yml](/configs/train.yml#L61-L93)

### Embedding and Projection Layers

The `__init__` method constructs five core parameter groups:

**Timestep embedding** — A frozen sinusoidal embedding table maps integer timestep indices ∈ [0, n_tsteps) to a `t_embed_dim`-dimensional vector using the standard positional encoding formula with base 1000. This embedding is never updated by gradients, ensuring the diffusion schedule remains fixed throughout training.

**Sequence-state projection** (`esm_s_mlp`) — A two-layer MLP with LayerNorm input and ReLU activation projects the concatenation of timestep embedding (32-dim) and torsion features (8-dim) into the sequence state dimension c_s. This is the critical bridge between the diffusion state and the transformer's internal representation.

**Pairwise-state projection** (`z_mlp`) — Similarly structured, this MLP projects the 2D distance-orientation featurization of noised coordinates into c_z. Its input dimension is `2 × DBINS + 6 + 1` (one-hot distance bins + sinusoidal orientation angles + RBF Ca–Ca features).

**Amino acid and secondary structure embeddings** — Two separate `nn.Embedding` tables map residue type and secondary structure class into c_s. The padding index is 0, and both use the shift-by-1 convention where 0 represents padding and valid indices start at 1.

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L37-L69), [tensor_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/tensor_utils.py#L116-L125)

## Forward Pass: From Diffusion State to Structure

The `forward` method implements the single-step denoising prediction. It accepts the current diffusion state (timestep `t`, torsion angles `alpha_t`, noised backbone `x_t`) and a batch dictionary containing sequence, secondary structure, mask, and residue indices.

### Step 1 — Sequence State Initialization

The initial per-residue hidden state `s_s_0` is assembled as a sum of three information streams:

```
s_s_0 = MLP( [sin_emb(t) ‖ α_t] ) + Embed_aa(aa) + Embed_ss(ss)
```

The timestep embedding and torsion features are concatenated along the feature dimension, projected through `esm_s_mlp`, then the amino acid and secondary structure embeddings are **additively combined**. This additive fusion ensures each signal can be independently interpreted by downstream attention layers rather than entangled through multiplicative interactions.

A notable training augmentation in `IDPForgeWrapper.training_step` randomly zeroes out secondary structure labels with 20% probability (`torch.rand(1).item() < 0.2`), forcing the model to learn robust predictions without relying on SS annotations.

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L110-L114), [wrapper.py](/idpforge/wrapper.py#L56-L83)

### Step 2 — Pairwise State Initialization

The noised backbone coordinates `x_t` (shape B × L × 5 × 3, representing N, Cα, C, O, Cβ atoms) are converted into a rich 2D feature map via `xyz_to_t2d`:

| Feature | Dimension | Computation |
|---|---|---|
| Cβ–Cβ distance one-hot | DBINS + 1 | Bucketized inter-residue distances |
| Cα–Cα RBF | DBINS | Gaussian radial basis functions |
| Orientation (sin/cos) | 6 | sin(ω), cos(ω), sin(θ), cos(θ), sin(φ), cos(φ) |

The distance features capture **global spatial proximity** while the orientation features (dihedral ω, θ and planar angle φ) encode **local frame relationships** between residue pairs. Together they provide the transformer with a geometric snapshot of the current noised conformation. The combined feature vector is projected through `z_mlp` to yield `s_z_0`.

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L117-L119), [tensor_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/tensor_utils.py#L147-L219)

### Step 3 — Recycling Feedback

If `prev_outputs` is provided (from a previous recycle iteration or self-conditioning), the model injects three recycling signals:

1. **Sequence recycle** — LayerNorm of the previous `s_s`, added to `s_s_0`
2. **Pairwise recycle** — LayerNorm of the previous `s_z`, added to `s_z_0`
3. **Distogram recycle** — A binned Cβ–Cβ distance histogram from the previous predicted coordinates, embedded into `s_z_0`

Self-conditioning during training is applied stochastically (50% probability when enabled): the model is run once at timestep t+1 with `torch.no_grad()` to obtain `prev_outputs`, which then condition the actual forward pass at timestep t. This teaches the network to leverage its own predictions as input, improving convergence during iterative sampling.

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L121-L129), [wrapper.py](/idpforge/wrapper.py#L64-L68)

### Step 4 — FoldingTrunk Execution

The initialized `s_s_0` and `s_z_0` are passed to `FoldingTrunk.forward`, which executes the main transformer loop:

1. **Relative positional embedding** added to pairwise state
2. **N × TriangularSelfAttentionBlock** iterations (with optional recycling)
3. **StructureModule** (IPA-based) converts final hidden states to 3D coordinates

The trunk returns a dictionary containing single/pair states, backbone frames, sidechain frames, torsion angles (normalized and unnormalized), and atom positions. The `IDPForge.forward` method filters this to the seven keys needed downstream, attaches atom masks and residue indices, and returns the structure prediction.

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L131-L153), [trunk.py](/esm/esmfold/trunk.py#L160-L227)

## TriangularSelfAttentionBlock

Each block implements the core information-processing primitive of the dual-track transformer. The computation proceeds through five sequential stages within a single block:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Block["TriangularSelfAttentionBlock"]
        direction TB
        A["1. Pair→Seq bias<br/>PairToSequence"] --> B["2. Seq self-attn<br/>(with pair bias)"]
        B --> C["3. Seq→Pair update<br/>SequenceToPair"]
        C --> D["4. Pair triangular<br/>mul + attn"]
        D --> E["5. Pair + Seq MLPs<br/>(ResidueMLP)"]
    end
```

### Stage 1 — Pair-to-Sequence Bias

`PairToSequence` applies LayerNorm to the pairwise state, then a linear projection from c_z to `num_heads`. The output serves as an **attention bias** added to the query-key dot products in the sequence self-attention, allowing pairwise geometric relationships to modulate which residues attend to each other.

### Stage 2 — Gated Sequence Self-Attention

A standard multi-head self-attention operates on the sequence state, enhanced by the pairwise bias from Stage 1. The attention mechanism uses a **gated output** where a sigmoid-activated linear projection of the input element-wise multiplies the attention output, providing a learned per-feature on/off switch. This gated attention is the same mechanism used in AlphaFold2's EvoFormer.

### Stage 3 — Sequence-to-Pair Update

`SequenceToPair` projects the updated sequence state through a linear layer, splits the result into query and key components, then computes both an **outer product** (q ⊙ k) and an **outer difference** (q − k) across all residue pairs. These are concatenated and projected to c_z, capturing both multiplicative and additive interactions between residue representations.

### Stage 4 — Triangular Pairwise Updates

Four operations update the pairwise state in sequence, all using **zero-initialized** final projections (ensuring the block starts as an identity mapping):

| Operation | OpenFold Component | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| Triangular multiplication (outgoing) | `TriangleMultiplicationOutgoing` | Row-wise aggregate → column broadcast |
| Triangular multiplication (incoming) | `TriangleMultiplicationIncoming` | Column-wise aggregate → row broadcast |
| Triangle attention (starting node) | `TriangleAttentionStartingNode` | Attend over rows |
| Triangle attention (ending node) | `TriangleAttentionEndingNode` | Attend over columns |

The triangular multiplication operations implement the **geometric reasoning** primitive from AlphaFold2: if residue i is close to j, and j is close to k, then information about the i–k relationship can be inferred through the intermediate node j. Row and column dropout (at 2× the base rate) provides regularization specific to each axial direction.

### Stage 5 — Residual MLPs

Both sequence and pairwise states pass through `ResidueMLP` modules (LayerNorm → Linear → ReLU → Linear → Dropout with residual connection), with inner dimension 4× the state dimension. These provide per-position feed-forward processing that refines the representations before the next block.

Sources: [tri_self_attn_block.py](/esm/esmfold/tri_self_attn_block.py#L26-L169), [misc.py](/esm/esmfold/misc.py#L120-L280)

## Zero Initialization Strategy

A critical architectural decision throughout the TriangularSelfAttentionBlock is **zero initialization** of all output projections. Every `linear_z`, `linear_o`, `o_proj`, and the final MLP layer in both `mlp_seq` and `mlp_pair` has its weights and biases initialized to zero. This means each block begins training as an approximate identity mapping, and the entire trunk initially passes its input featurization directly to the structure module. This stabilizes early training by ensuring the network starts from a well-conditioned baseline rather than random projections.

Sources: [tri_self_attn_block.py](/esm/esmfold/tri_self_attn_block.py#L88-L105)

## Iterative Denoising: The `recon` Method

While `forward` performs a single denoising step, `recon` orchestrates the **full reverse diffusion trajectory** from T → 0. It iterates backward through timesteps, calling `forward` at each step and delegating coordinate/torsion updates to the external `denoiser` object:

```python
for t in range(n_tsteps - 1, end_tsteps, -int(n_tsteps / inf_tsteps)):
```

Three conditioning mechanisms operate within this loop:

**Template conditioning** — When `template_cfg` is provided, residues covered by the template mask are force-set to timestep 0 with their template coordinates and torsions, ensuring folded regions remain anchored while disordered regions diffuse freely. See [IDR Sampling with Folded Templates](13-idr-sampling-with-folded-templates).

**Experimental guidance** — When a `potential` is active, gradient-based corrections are applied to the denoised prediction: `p_x0 += clamp(x_grad × scaler(t), max=clip)`. The scaler follows a configurable decay schedule (constant, linear, or quadratic), amplifying guidance at late timesteps when the structure is nearly formed. See [Experimental Guidance Potentials](14-experimental-guidance-potentials).

**Self-conditioning** — When enabled, the output from each denoising step is fed back as `prev_outputs` for the next step, creating a progressive refinement loop within the reverse diffusion itself.

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L155-L208)

## The `sample` Method: End-to-End Inference

The `sample` method provides the complete public API for generating conformations. It handles sequence/secondary-structure encoding (with multi-chain support via glycine linkers and residue-index offsets), tensor collation, optional masking patterns, potential initialization, and delegates to `recon`. The output dictionary contains final atom positions, residue types, atom masks, and the secondary structure assignment — ready for PDB writing or downstream scoring.

The `initialize_potential` factory supports both single-potential and composite (weighted multi-potential) configurations, with the decay schedule controlling how strongly experimental data guides the denoising at each timestep.

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L211-L269)

## Training Wrapper: IDPForgeWrapper

The `IDPForgeWrapper` PyTorch Lightning module wraps `IDPForge` with training infrastructure:

| Component | Implementation |
|---|---|
| **Optimizer** | Adam with AlphaFold-style LR scheduler (warmup + decay) |
| **EMA** | Exponential Moving Average applied before zeroing gradients; loaded for validation, restored after |
| **Validation** | Full reverse diffusion (`model.recon`) with composite loss: weighted sum of CA-DRMSD, violation, Cβ distance, and Rg error |
| **Checkpointing** | EMA state dict saved/loaded alongside model weights |

The training step applies two stochastic augmentations beyond standard data loading: (1) random SS dropout (20% chance of replacing all SS labels with the masked class), and (2) self-conditioning (50% chance when enabled, only when not at the final timestep). Loss computation delegates to [Loss Functions](10-loss-functions) which combines FAPE, angular, distance, and violation terms.

Sources: [wrapper.py](/idpforge/wrapper.py#L17-L208)

## Secondary Structure Taxonomy

IDPForge defines 8 secondary structure classes that extend the standard DSSP alphabet with disorder-specific categories:

| Index | Symbol | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | H | α-helix |
| 1 | E | β-strand |
| 2 | P | Polyproline helix |
| 3 | A | α-helix coil |
| 4 | B | β-bridge coil |
| 5 | C | Coil (generic) |
| 6 | L | Loop |
| 7 | − | Masked / unknown |

The coil subtypes (A, B, C, L) are sampled according to learned probabilities {A: 0.3, B: 0.5, L: 0.1, C: 0.1} when no explicit Ramachandran-based assignment is available. This granular SS vocabulary provides the transformer with richer structural priors than a binary ordered/disordered label.

Sources: [definitions.py](/idpforge/utils/definitions.py#L9-L14), [misc.py](/idpforge/misc.py#L55-L73)

## Memory-Efficient Inference

The `set_chunk_size` method enables **axial attention chunking**, reducing memory complexity from O(L²) to approximately O(L) by processing the triangular attention dimensions in fixed-size chunks. This is essential for sampling long disordered regions where sequence lengths can exceed 500 residues. The chunk size is propagated to all TriangularSelfAttentionBlock instances within the trunk.

> [!TIP]
> When configuring the trunk for IDP sampling, the default ESMFold-scale architecture (48 blocks, c_s=1024, c_z=128) is intentionally reduced to 2 blocks with c_s=128, c_z=64. This ~200× parameter reduction is possible because the diffusion framework decomposes the mapping from sequence to structure into many small denoising steps, each requiring far less representational capacity than a single-shot prediction.

> [!TIP]
> The zero-initialized output projections in every TriangularSelfAttentionBlock mean the trunk initially acts as a passthrough — the structure module receives the raw featurized inputs on the first forward pass. This architectural choice eliminates the need for careful learning-rate warmup specific to the transformer blocks and allows the diffusion timestep embedding to immediately influence predictions from step 0 of training.

Sources: [model.py](/idpforge/model.py#L272-L278), [trunk.py](/esm/esmfold/trunk.py#L153-L158)

## Architectural Relationship to Subsystems

The IDPForge Transformer Network sits at the center of three interacting subsystems. Its **inputs** are prepared by [SE(3) Backbone Diffusion](6-se-3-backbone-diffusion) and [SO(3) Rotational Diffusion](7-so-3-rotational-diffusion) (which generate the noised coordinates and rotations), plus [Torsion Angle Diffusion](8-torsion-angle-diffusion) (which provides α_t). Its **outputs** are consumed by the denoiser during [IDP Sampling](12-idp-sampling-fully-disordered) or [IDR Sampling](13-idr-sampling-with-folded-templates), and its **training** is governed by the loss functions and data pipeline documented in [Loss Functions](10-loss-functions) and [Data Loading and Noising](11-data-loading-and-noising).

# SE(3) Backbone Diffusion



IDPForge generates intrinsically disordered protein conformers by reversing a structured diffusion process over the **SE(3)** manifold—the group of rigid-body transformations (rotation + translation) that govern backbone atom placement. Rather than diffusing raw Cartesian coordinates as a monolithic ℝ³ᴺ problem, IDPForge **factorizes SE(3) into its rotation group SO(3) and translation group ℝ³**, applying the Isotropic Gaussian on SO(3) (IGSO(3)) for backbone frame rotations and a standard Gaussian kernel for Cα translations. This factorization preserves the geometric structure of peptide frames during both noising and denoising, yielding physically plausible intermediate states at every timestep. A third diffusion channel over sidechain torsion angles (SO(2)⁴) operates in parallel, completing the full backbone-and-sidechain generative process.

## Mathematical Foundation

The SE(3) group is the semi-direct product **SE(3) = SO(3) ⋊ ℝ³**, meaning every rigid transformation decomposes into a rotation R ∈ SO(3) followed by a translation t ∈ ℝ³. IDPForge exploits this by defining three independent diffusion channels that are jointly applied during the forward process and sequentially composed during reverse inference:

| Channel | Manifold | Distribution | Parameters | Implementation |
|---------|----------|-------------|------------|----------------|
| **Backbone Rotation** | SO(3) | IGSO(3) — Isotropic Gaussian | σ(t) schedule: min_σ=0.05, min_b=1.5, max_b=2.5 | `IGSO3` class |
| **Cα Translation** | ℝ³ | Isotropic Gaussian (DDPM) | Linear β schedule: β₀=0.01, β_T=0.06–0.08 | `EuclideanDiffuser` class |
| **Sidechain Torsion** | SO(2)⁴ | Wrapped Gaussian | Linear β schedule: β₀=0.01, β_T=0.06 | `TorsionDiffuser` class |

The IGSO(3) density at rotation angle ω with variance parameter t is computed via the truncated power series (Leach et al. 2022, Equation 5):

**f(ω, t) = Σ_{l=0}^{L} (2l+1) · exp(−l(l+1)t/2) · sin(ω(l+½)) / sin(ω/2)**

where L=2000 is the truncation level and the reparameterization σ = √2·ε aligns IGSO(3) with Brownian motion on SO(3) under the canonical inner product ⟨u, v⟩_SO3 = Trace(uvᵀ)/2.

Sources: [igso3_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/igso3_utils.py#L42-L64), [diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L303-L314)

## Architecture: Diffusion Hierarchy

The diffusion system is organized as a class hierarchy where the top-level `Diffuser` orchestrates the three sub-diffusers, and the `Denoiser` coordinates the reverse process. The following diagram captures the ownership and data-flow relationships:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Diffuser {
        +T: int
        +crd_scale: float
        +so3_diffuser: IGSO3
        +eucl_diffuser: EuclideanDiffuser
        +tor_diffuser: TorsionDiffuser
        +diffuse_pose(xyz, sequence, diffusion_mask)
    }
    class IGSO3 {
        +T: int
        +min_sigma: float
        +min_b: float
        +max_b: float
        +igso3_vals: dict
        +sigma(t) float
        +g(t) float
        +sample_vec(ts, n_samples)
        +diffuse_frames(xyz, diffusion_mask)
        +"reverse_sample_vectorized(R_t, R_0, t, noise_level)"
        +score_norm(t, omega)
    }
    class EuclideanDiffuser {
        +T: int
        +"beta_schedule: ndarray"
        +diffuse_translations(xyz, diffusion_mask)
        +"apply_kernel_recursive(xyz, diffusion_mask)"
    }
    class TorsionDiffuser {
        +T: int
        +"beta_schedule: ndarray"
        +diffuse_torsions(torsions, diffusion_mask)
    }
    class Denoiser {
        +T: int
        +diffuser: Diffuser
        +noise_schedule_ca(t)
        +noise_schedule_frame(t)
        +"trans_alphabar: ndarray"
        +"tor_alphabar: ndarray"
        +init_samples(sequences)
        +"get_next_pose(x_t, px_0, tor_t, ptor_0, t, ...)"
    }
    Diffuser --> IGSO3 : so3_diffuser
    Diffuser --> EuclideanDiffuser : eucl_diffuser
    Diffuser --> TorsionDiffuser : tor_diffuser
    Denoiser --> Diffuser : diffuser
```

The `Diffuser` is constructed with the total number of timesteps T (default 200) and schedule parameters for each channel. Each sub-diffuser pre-computes its noise schedule at initialization. The `Denoiser` wraps the `Diffuser` and additionally pre-computes the cumulative alpha-bar schedules needed for the reverse posterior distributions.

Sources: [diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L491-L517), [diff_utils.py](/idpforge/utils/diff_utils.py#L574-L607)

## Forward Process: Noising a Protein Structure

The forward diffusion transforms a ground-truth protein structure into noise through T sequential steps. The `diffuse_pose` method orchestrates this by decomposing the input coordinates into frames, translations, and torsions, then applying each sub-diffuser independently.

### Frame Extraction

Backbone frames (rotation matrices) are extracted from the N–Cα–C atoms of each residue via Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization. Given coordinates for backbone atoms N, Cα, C, the rotation matrix R is constructed as:

- **e₁** = (C − Cα) / ‖C − Cα‖  
- **e₂** = normalize((N − Cα) − ⟨N − Cα, e₁⟩·e₁)  
- **e₃** = e₁ × e₂  
- **R** = [e₁ | e₂ | e₃]

This yields an SO(3) element per residue that encodes the local backbone orientation.

### Rotation Diffusion via IGSO(3)

At each timestep t, rotation vectors are sampled from IGSO(3) using inverse CDF sampling over the pre-computed discrete distribution. The sampled rotation is applied via left-multiplication to the true frame: **R_perturbed = R_sampled · R_true**. The perturbed coordinates are reconstructed by rotating the local backbone atoms around Cα: **xyz_perturbed = R_sampled · (xyz − Cα) + Cα**.

### Translation Diffusion

Cα positions are noised through a standard DDPM forward kernel with linear β schedule. At each step t, the kernel applies: **x_t = √(1−β_t) · x_{t−1} + √β_t · ε**, where ε ~ N(0, I). The `apply_kernel_recursive` method applies this T times, accumulating translational deltas. Coordinates are scaled by `crd_scale=0.25` before noising to normalize the spatial scale.

### Combined Noised Output
